The '''2015–16 Bundesliga''' was the 53rd season of the [[Bundesliga]], [[Germany]]'s premier [[association football|football]] competition. The season started on 14 August 2015 and ended on 14 May 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co12/se18336/all-matches/ |title=Bundesliga 2015/2016 » Schedule |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref> [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] were the defending champions, after winning their 24th Bundesliga title and 25th German championship overall in the previous season.

Bayern Munich won the 2015–16 title in the second-last round on 7 May 2016, thereby becoming the first club in the history of the Bundesliga and the [[List of German football champions|German football championship]] to win four consecutive championships.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.welt.de/newsticker/news1/article155135199/Bundesliga-Rekord-Titelgewinn-fuer-FC-Bayern.html |title=Bundesliga: Rekord-Titelgewinn für FC Bayern|date=7 May 2016 |website=welt.de |publisher=[[Die Welt]]|access-date= 8 May 2016|language=de|trans-title=Bundesliga: Record title for FC Bayern}}</ref>

A total of 18 teams were participating in this year's edition of the Bundesliga. Of these, 15 sides qualified directly from the [[2014–15 Bundesliga|2014–15 season]] and the two sides were directly promoted from the [[2014–15 2. Bundesliga|2014–15 2. Bundesliga season]]: [[FC Ingolstadt 04|FC Ingolstadt]], the champions, and [[SV Darmstadt 98|Darmstadt 98]], the runners-up. The final participant was decided by a [[2014–15 Bundesliga#Relegation play-offs|two-legged play-off]], in which the 16th-placed Bundesliga club, [[Hamburger SV]], defeated the third-place finisher in the [[2. Bundesliga]], [[Karlsruher SC]].

==Relegation play-offs==
The team which finished 16th faced the third-placed [[2015–16 2. Bundesliga]] side for a two-legged play-off. The winner on [[Playoff format#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregate]] score after both matches will earn entry into the 2016–17 Bundesliga.
